stories.title: DGCA gives SpiceJet one week to improve
stories.summary: The Directorate General of Civil Aviation has issued a show-cause notice to SpiceJet, demanding an operational plan within seven days. The airline currently operates fewer than 20 daily flights, with three in four domestic services delayed or cancelled. The regulator has yet to ban ticket sales.

stories.summary: Mumbai: The Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA) has issued a seven-day show-cause notice to SpiceJet, seeking explanations for mounting flight cancellations, operational disruptions, delayed payments to service providers and alleged regulatory violations, as the cash-strapped airline struggles to keep a significant part of its fleet operational. stories.title: Air India board reviews fuel costs and integration
stories.summary: The board of Air India met to discuss operational challenges, specifically rising fuel costs and airspace restrictions. The airline is currently pursuing an integration plan with Air India Express to improve cost effectiveness. The carrier continues to work on its transformation strategy amid ongoing financial headwinds.

IndiGo launches direct Mumbai to Dar es Salaam service
stories.summary: IndiGo has inaugurated a daily non-stop service between Mumbai and Dar es Salaam, Tanzania. The route marks the airline's latest expansion into East Africa. The inaugural flight departed Mumbai early Friday morning, further strengthening direct aviation links between the two regions.

stories.title: DGCA sends show cause notice to SpiceJet, flags violations, grounded fleet
stories.summary: DGCA has given SpiceJet seven days to respond to a show-cause notice flagging eight instances of alleged regulatory and operational lapses, including repeated flight cancellations, failure to operate approved schedules and delayed payments to service providers. stories.title: IndiGo adds daily non-stop Delhi-Kuala Lumpur flights to boost Southeast Asia connectivity
stories.summary: IndiGo, one of India's biggest airlines and one of the fastest-growing carriers in the world, has announced expansion of its Southeast Asia connectivity from Delhi, ahead of the year-end holidays.According to the official release, IndiGo will launch daily, non-stop flights between Delhi and Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia, from December 20, additional

stories.title: Ethiopian Airlines investigates ShebaMiles data breach
stories.summary: Ethiopian Airlines is investigating a cybersecurity incident involving its ShebaMiles loyalty program, which held over 5.38 million accounts last year. The airline stated that financial data remains secure and flight operations were not disrupted. The investigation into the limited scope incident is currently underway.

stories.title: Lufthansa plans 1,000 job cuts to fix losses
stories.summary: Lufthansa Airlines intends to cut 1,000 full-time jobs at its Frankfurt and Munich hubs and reduce its fleet of Airbus A320-family jets. The airline is attempting to address persistent losses that previous turnaround measures failed to fix. Specific details on the implementation of these cuts remain unpublished.

stories.title: JetBlue expands at Fort Lauderdale following Spirit shutdown
stories.summary: JetBlue is adding daily flights to Tegucigalpa and Grand Cayman from Fort Lauderdale, targeting international routes previously served by Spirit Airlines. The expansion consolidates JetBlue’s position as the airport's largest carrier, following its initial focus on domestic routes after Spirit ceased operations in May.

stories.title: United Airlines briefly claims top spot in global rankings
stories.summary: United Airlines is set to become the world's largest carrier for one day on November 26. OAG data shows US passenger services will drop by 44 percent for the Thanksgiving holiday, leaving United as the largest operator while other airlines significantly reduce their scheduled flights.

stories.title: Frontier Airlines offers unlimited annual pass for $399
stories.summary: Frontier Airlines has launched its 2027 GoWild Annual Pass, promising unlimited flights with no blackout dates for a $399 flat fee. While the pass allows travel through the end of 2027, the airline notes that additional charges may be applied to individual tickets.

stories.title: Delta CEO cites rising costs despite higher airfares
stories.summary: Delta Air Lines CEO Ed Bastian stated that the carrier is earning less money than a year ago, citing rising fuel, labor, and airport costs. Despite recent increases in ticket prices, Bastian noted that these expenses continue to pressure the airline's bottom line.

stories.title: IAG faces softer UK aviation market as UBS flags slowdown in airline capacity
stories.summary: International Consolidated Airlines Group faces a weakening UK aviation market after UBS data showed flight capacity fell 1% in the first two weeks of November. The decline reversed October growth and reflected a broader global slowdown. Italy and Spain continue to outperform Britain, France and Germany.

stories.title: I flew the world's best airline in business class
stories.summary: A passenger on Singapore Airlines described the 19-hour flight from the US to Singapore as a luxury experience featuring private seats and restaurant-quality meals. The route is the world's second-longest by distance, though the traveler noted the journey did not feel long at all.

stories.title: Turkish Airlines boosts mainland China presence with Istanbul-Chengdu nonstop route
stories.summary: Turkish Airlines has launched a thrice-weekly nonstop service to Chengdu using a Boeing 787-9 Dreamliner. This marks the carrier's fourth gateway in mainland China. The city of 21 million residents hosts a significant roster of multinationals across the electronics, automotive and aviation sectors.

stories.title: Air New Zealand faces criminal charges over compensation
stories.summary: The Commerce Commission has filed criminal charges against Air New Zealand under the Fair Trading Act. The regulator alleges the airline misled passengers regarding compensation for delayed or canceled flights, claiming the carrier incorrectly capped payouts and restricted expenses that passengers were legally entitled to claim.

stories.title: Textron to sell industrial units to focus on aerospace
stories.summary: Textron has agreed to sell its Kautex and Specialized Vehicles businesses to Kingswood Capital Management for $1.2 billion. The company intends to become a pure-play aerospace and defense firm. The transaction is expected to close in the first half of 2027, generating $1.1 billion in net cash.

stories.title: Malaysia Airlines closes in on the Boeing 787-10 to renew its widebody fleet
stories.summary: Malaysia Airlines is acquiring 20 Boeing 787 Dreamliners to replace its seven Airbus A350-900s. The airline has not operated Boeing widebodies since 2016. Deliveries are expected from 2031, though the CEO warned that industry delays threaten the carrier's plan to grow 8% by 2027.

stories.title: Philippine Airlines firms up an order for 15 Boeing 787-10 Dreamliners
stories.summary: Philippine Airlines has finalized an order for 15 Boeing 787-10 jets with an option for five more. The deal represents the airline's largest-ever widebody purchase. The aircraft will be powered by GE Aerospace engines, marking a milestone in the 80-year partnership between the airline and Boeing.

stories.title: Textron's $1.2B sale marks shift to aerospace and defense
stories.summary: Textron confirmed the sale of its industrial arm to a Kingswood Capital Management affiliate for $1.2 billion. The move aims to consolidate the firm's focus on its core aviation and defense franchises. Upon completion in 2027, the company will rebrand as a pure-play aerospace entity.

stories.title: Emirates Pushes Airbus to Revive A380 With 100-Jet Order - AirGuide Business
Middle East Airlines gets its first Airbus A321XLR
stories.summary: Middle East Airlines has taken delivery of its first Airbus A321XLR, seven years after placing the initial order. The carrier was the launch customer for the type in 2019 but faced delivery delays that allowed other airlines to receive the aircraft first. Patience is a requirement.

stories.title: Middle East Airlines takes delivery of first Airbus A321XLR
stories.summary: Middle East Airlines has received the first of five Airbus A321XLR aircraft. The airline, which was the first to order the type in 2019, plans to use the narrowbody for both regional sectors and longer, thinner routes. The delivery expands the carrier's all-Airbus fleet.

stories.title: OIG launches first audit of FAA supplier oversight since 2008
stories.summary: The Transportation Department's Office of Inspector General plans to audit the FAA's oversight of production approval holders. The review follows recent signs of weakened surveillance of manufacturers and suppliers. The audit is the first of its kind in 18 years.

stories.title: IndiGo cancels flights to Saudi Arabia amid security concerns
stories.summary: IndiGo has suspended all flights to and from Jeddah, Madinah, Riyadh and Dammam until November 30. The airline cited the prevailing security situation following reports of intercepted ballistic missiles. Passengers are being offered assistance as the carrier prioritizes the safety of crew and travelers.

stories.title: Air India suspends Jeddah, Riyadh and Dammam flights
stories.summary: Air India and Air India Express have suspended flights to Jeddah until November 24 and to Riyadh and Dammam until November 30. The airline cited the regional security situation and is offering affected passengers complimentary rescheduling or full refunds upon cancellation.

stories.title: Security officials warn US aviation industry of Al Qaeda attack calls
stories.summary: US security agencies have warned airlines and airports of public messaging from Al Qaeda supporters praising a recent attempted hijacking. The FBI and DHS report encourages similar attacks against US and Israeli interests. The industry has been alerted to the potential for copycat incidents.

stories.title: Air India and Air India Express extend Saudi flight cancellations
stories.summary: Air India Group has extended the suspension of flights to Jeddah until November 24, while services to Riyadh and Dammam remain grounded until November 30. The airline stated the decision follows ongoing regional instability. Customers may opt for refunds or rescheduling for bookings made before November 20.

stories.title: Mexico Likely to Keep US Aviation Safety Rating, Airport Operator Says - U.S. News & World Report
FAA completes India aviation safety oversight review
stories.summary: The FAA has finished a five-day assessment of India's aviation safety oversight system. The review examined airworthiness standards, personnel licensing and aircraft operations. Findings from the IASA program evaluation are expected following further consultations between the FAA and the Directorate General of Civil Aviation.

stories.title: FAA completes audit of India's aviation safety oversight standards
stories.summary: The US Federal Aviation Administration completed a five-day audit of India's aviation safety oversight, focusing on aircraft operations and personnel licensing. The Directorate General of Civil Aviation was debriefed on the findings. Final results are expected in a few months. India remains a fast-growing civil aviation market.

stories.title: FAA investigates nationwide ground stop
stories.summary: The FAA ordered a nationwide ground stop on November 13 after network instability affected 17 air traffic control centers. The agency identified excessive traffic at equipment locations in Texas and Arkansas as a possible cause. Approximately 3,500 airborne aircraft were allowed to reach their destinations safely.

stories.title: India's air safety radar picks up gaps in ageing ATC automation systems
stories.summary: Mumbai air traffic controllers are currently using commercial television screens to manage flight information and alerts. The Airports Authority of India previously awarded a contract for new automation systems to replace ageing infrastructure. Controllers report that the current setup makes it difficult to read critical flight data.

stories.title: Ahmedabad Air India crash probe nearing completion
stories.summary: The Supreme Court granted the Centre two weeks to conclude the investigation into the June 2025 Ahmedabad plane crash that killed 260 people. Solicitor General Tushar Mehta stated that the probe is at the final stage. Families of the deceased have sought an independent, court-monitored investigation.

stories.title: Ahmedabad Air India crash probe nearing completion
stories.summary: The Central government told the Supreme Court that the investigation into the June 2025 Ahmedabad plane crash is nearing completion. Solicitor General Tushar Mehta requested a three-week adjournment to finalize the process. The court is reviewing petitions from families and safety organizations regarding the tragedy.

stories.title: Hubballi Airport to get second pilot training academy
stories.summary: Hubballi Airport will host a second flight training academy after Dayalans Aviation Pvt Ltd secured approval from the Airports Authority of India. Operations are expected to begin within six months. The airport director cited high demand as the primary reason for expanding the site's training infrastructure.

stories.title: Centre approves 11 new flying training organisations to boost India’s pilot training capacity - DD News
K-State Salina Selected for National NOAA Pilot Training Program - KCLY Radio
UND selected for NOAA aviation partnership
stories.summary: The University of North Dakota has been named one of three universities to establish a Cooperative Aviation Center with the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration. The partnership creates a pathway for students to fly scientific research aircraft, including those used for hurricane reconnaissance and atmospheric studies.

stories.title: FAA reports outcomes for Vets2Wings pilot program
stories.summary: The FAA reported that its Vets2Wings program has produced 39 graduates and currently supports 66 active students. Since 2022, participants have obtained 192 pilot certificates and ratings. The initiative provides financial and career support to military veterans pursuing civilian pilot qualifications through the University of North Dakota.

stories.title: JetBlue welcomes 40 new first officers
stories.summary: JetBlue has added 40 newly hired first officers to its Class 01-26. The pilots will undergo initial qualification training to support staffing requirements across the airline's Airbus fleet. As of September 2026, the company reported an operating fleet of 298 aircraft.

stories.title: US Air Force pilot training hits 1,518 graduates
stories.summary: The US Air Force graduated 1,518 new pilots in fiscal year 2026, the highest number in 35 years. The service reached its target of 1,500 graduates for the first time since 1991. The figures were confirmed by the commander of Air Education and Training Command.

stories.title: US Air Force hires XStar to fly HondaJets for bomber training
stories.summary: The US Air Force has contracted XStar to operate HondaJet aircraft for B-1B bomber pilot training. The program aims to improve complex decision-making and prepare crews for long-duration flights. Using civilian business jets is intended to shift flight hours away from more costly frontline military aircraft.
